-- The right-click-menu explanations the detailed-tooltip fork shows in place of the unit -- lines (BenillaUnitFrame_OnEnter below) — ref GlobalStrings.lua l.2993/3081/2754/2755 -- (enUS), fallback form: the real localized GlobalStrings.lua runs before this file at -- runtime (ui_script/mod.rs), so these only fill in for the tests. CombatText.xml's shape. PARTY_OPTIONS_LABEL = PARTY_OPTIONS_LABEL or "Party Options" PLAYER_OPTIONS_LABEL = PLAYER_OPTIONS_LABEL or "Player Options" NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PARTYOPTIONS = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PARTYOPTIONS or "If you belong to a party, you can right-click your portrait to bring up the Party Options menu. This menu will allow you to quit the party or see what looting rules the party is using. A party leader can add or remove party members, as well as change the party's looting rules." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PLAYEROPTIONS = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PLAYEROPTIONS or "Right-click to bring up special commands for interacting with another player. You can inspect their equipment, issue a party invite, initiate a trade, or challenge a player to a duel. A group leader can promote or remove that player from the group."
-- The client's PowerBarColor values, keyed by the UnitPowerType token. BENILLA_POWER_COLORS = { MANA = { r = 0.0, g = 0.0, b = 1.0 }, RAGE = { r = 1.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0 }, FOCUS = { r = 1.0, g = 0.5, b = 0.25 }, ENERGY = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 0.0 }, HAPPINESS = { r = 0.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0 }, }
-- The client's UnitReactionColor table (ref-TargetFrame.lua l.6-14), indexed by -- UnitReaction 1..8 (hated..exalted): 1-2 red, 3 orange, 4 neutral yellow, 5-7 green. The -- name-plate reaction tint (TargetFrame_CheckFaction) reads it — this is what makes a neutral -- beast's plate yellow, a hostile's red, a friendly's green. BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS = { { r = 1.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0 }, { r = 1.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0 }, { r = 1.0, g = 0.5, b = 0.0 }, { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 0.0 }, { r = 0.0, g = 1.0, b = 0.0 }, { r = 0.0, g = 1.0, b = 0.0 }, { r = 0.0, g = 1.0, b = 0.0 }, }
-- Wire an instance to its unit token (called from each frame's OnLoad), cache its child -- widgets, register the event set, and do the first paint. deadText is target-only -- (getglobal returns nil for the player, which has no DEAD region) — guarded at use. function BenillaUnitFrame_OnLoad(frame, unit) frame.unit = unit local name = frame:GetName() frame.healthBar = getglobal(name .. "HealthBar") frame.powerBar = getglobal(name .. "PowerBar") -- The name/level/dead text live inside $parentTextureFrame (so they draw over the ring art -- that draws over the bars), so their global names carry the TextureFrame prefix. local tf = name .. "TextureFrame" -- The recessed-bar look, the reference's own mechanism (ref-TargetFrame.lua l.32-34): -- push the bars one frame level BELOW the ring art's TextureFrame. Frame level is the -- only key term above the draw layer (decision 0884), so this is the only thing that can -- hold a BACKGROUND ring texture over an ARTWORK bar fill. See the LAYERING note up top. local textureFrameLevel = getglobal(tf):GetFrameLevel() frame.healthBar:SetFrameLevel(textureFrameLevel - 1) frame.powerBar:SetFrameLevel(textureFrameLevel - 1) frame.nameText = getglobal(tf .. "NameText") frame.levelText = getglobal(tf .. "LevelText") frame.deadText = getglobal(tf .. "DeadText") -- Target-only (the "??" skull on the level slot); getglobal returns nil for the -- player, guarded at use. frame.highLevel = getglobal(tf .. "HighLevelTexture") -- Target-only (the level/name plate); getglobal returns nil for the player, guarded at use. frame.nameBackground = getglobal(name .. "NameBackground") -- The live model portrait (the real API's global, ref-UnitFrame.lua): bind the portrait -- region to this frame's unit token; the app renders that unit's model off-screen and feeds -- the bake back into the region (crates/benilla/src/portrait.rs). The binding is a token, so -- one call suffices — the app keeps the image current per token (it re-bakes on target / -- model change), which is why the ref's UNIT_PORTRAIT_UPDATE re-call isn't needed here (the -- event joins the surface when addon parity wants it). Until a bake lands (no unit / model -- still loading) the circle is simply empty. frame.portrait = getglobal(name .. "Portrait") SetPortraitTexture(frame.portrait, unit) -- The PvP flag icon (decision 0646), under the TextureFrame like the ring art it -- draws over — see BenillaUnitFrame_UpdatePvP. frame.pvpIcon = getglobal(tf .. "PVPIcon") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXHEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_LEVEL") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_POWER_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_NAME_UPDATE") -- The PvP icon's repaint wire (decision 0646 §2) — in the reference exactly the three -- frames that draw the icon register it (PlayerFrame, TargetFrame, PartyMemberFrame) -- and nothing else does. frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_FACTION") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED") -- The aura rows and the classification border are target-only (ref TargetFrame_OnLoad -- registers UNIT_AURA and UNIT_CLASSIFICATION_CHANGED; PlayerFrame registers neither, -- and there is no CheckClassification for the player — your own frame never wears a -- dragon). The ring-art region is the one the border swap re-textures, so only the -- target caches the handle: its presence is what gates the swap in Update, the same -- nil-handle idiom highLevel/nameBackground use above. if unit == "target" then frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_AURA") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_CLASSIFICATION_CHANGED") frame.frameTexture = getglobal(tf .. "Texture") end -- The portrait hit indicator (decision 0576): only the player frame registers -- UNIT_COMBAT in 1.12 (ref PlayerFrame_OnLoad — the target frame has no feedback -- text). Ref: CombatFeedback_Initialize(PlayerHitIndicator, 30). if unit == "player" then frame.feedbackText = getglobal(tf .. "HitIndicator") frame.feedbackFontHeight = 30 frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_COMBAT") -- The status flash (ref PlayerFrame_OnLoad, decision 1082): the resting zzz / -- auto-attack swords under the portrait, the gold/red ring, and the pulse -- counters. Handles cached like pvpIcon above; their presence is what gates -- BenillaPlayerFrame_UpdateStatus in the shared Update. frame.statusTexture = getglobal(tf .. "StatusTexture") frame.attackBackground = getglobal(tf .. "AttackBackground") frame.restIcon = getglobal(tf .. "RestIcon") frame.attackIcon = getglobal(tf .. "AttackIcon") frame.statusGlow = getglobal(name .. "StatusGlow") frame.restGlow = getglobal(name .. "StatusGlowRestGlow") frame.attackGlow = getglobal(name .. "StatusGlowAttackGlow") frame.statusCounter = 0 frame.statusSign = -1 frame.attackBackground:SetVertexColor(0.8, 0.1, 0.1) frame.attackBackground:SetAlpha(0.4) -- Its four wires (ref PlayerFrame_OnLoad's registrations): auto-attack toggling -- (ENTER/LEAVE_COMBAT), the aggro list (REGEN_DISABLED/ENABLED), and the rest -- flag (UPDATE_RESTING); PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD is registered above for all units. frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTER_COMBAT") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LEAVE_COMBAT") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_UPDATE_RESTING") end -- A plain Frame isn't mouse-enabled by construction (only Button/EditBox are); enable it so -- the hover tooltip fires (the real client's unit frames take the mouse to target/tooltip). frame:EnableMouse(true) BenillaUnitFrame_Update(frame) end
-- Hover: the engine's SetUnit — the byte-verified unit line law (decision 0276: name/ -- subtitle/level composition/PvP/Skinnable + the health bar), then the ref's reaction -- recolor of line 1 (ref UnitFrame_OnEnter l.68-76: the FrameXML half of the split). -- The plate goes to the DEFAULT corner, not beside the frame — ref UnitFrame_OnEnter -- l.56 is GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, this): unit-frame tooltips live at -- the screen's bottom-right like world hovers. (The TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME re-poll is not -- ours: the engine's health watcher is the live half of it, and name/level don't drift -- mid-hover yet.) -- -- The DETAILED-TOOLTIP FORK (ref UnitFrame_OnEnter l.58-67, director-approved 0663) is the -- surprising half: with tips on — 1.12's default, decision 0661 — the frame explains its -- RIGHT-CLICK MENU instead of the unit, and returns BEFORE SetUnit, so the health/level -- lines never render at all. Your own portrait always takes it; another player's takes it -- whenever they're your target. The ref excepts PartyMemberFrame1-4 by name; ours are a -- separate file with their own OnEnter (PartyFrame.xml), so there is nothing to except here. -- -- One divergence, named: the ref gates the second branch on UnitPlayerControlled("target"), -- which is true for a player OR a player's pet/charm. This engine has no such binding and no -- flag to build one from — UnitIsPlayer is the nearest honest read, so a charmed mob or -- another player's pet falls through to the unit tooltip where the reference would explain -- the menu. The player case, which is the one anybody hovers, is exact. -- ref UnitFrame_OnEnter l.55-57, ahead of everything else: the ONLY lit/grey cursor split -- over a UI element in 1.12, and it is authored here in Lua rather than in the engine -- (wow-re item-target-cursor-and-dropitemonunit.md 4.3). Bag and paper-doll slots have no -- such branch, which is why they show the ordinary pointer. function BenillaUnitFrame_OnEnter(frame) local unit = frame.unit if SpellIsTargeting() then if SpellCanTargetUnit(unit) then SetCursor("CAST_CURSOR") else SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end end if not UnitExists(unit) then return end GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, frame) if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS == "1" then if frame:GetName() == "BenillaPlayerFrame" then GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(frame, PARTY_OPTIONS_LABEL, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PARTYOPTIONS) return elseif UnitIsPlayer("target") and not UnitIsUnit("target", "player") and not UnitIsUnit("target", "pet") then GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(frame, PLAYER_OPTIONS_LABEL, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PLAYEROPTIONS) return end end if GameTooltip:SetUnit(unit) then getglobal("GameTooltipTextLeft1"):SetTextColor(GameTooltip_UnitColor(unit)) end end
-- ref UnitFrame_OnLeave l.84-88: the fade is the tips-OFF branch. With detailed tips on the -- plate HIDES outright — the ref's own pairing, and the right one: an explanation that -- lingers on a ramp reads as a stuck tooltip, where a unit readout fading is the client's -- signature. (Items Hide, units fade — that split still holds for the world mouseover.) function BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave(frame) -- ref UnitFrame_OnLeave l.86: leaving a unit frame while still targeting goes to the -- GREY cast cursor, not to the base one — you have left the only thing the armed spell -- could have bound. if SpellIsTargeting() then SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS == "1" then GameTooltip:Hide() else GameTooltip:FadeOut() end end
function BenillaUnitFrame_OnEvent(frame) -- UNIT_* events name their unit in arg1; ignore other units' updates. if string.sub(event, 1, 5) == "UNIT_" and arg1 ~= frame.unit then return end -- The hit-indicator feed (ref PlayerFrame_OnEvent's UNIT_COMBAT arm): no repaint — -- the event carries feedback, not state. if event == "UNIT_COMBAT" then CombatFeedback_OnCombatEvent(frame, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5) return end -- The status flash's state arms (ref PlayerFrame_OnEvent l.100-115, decision 1082): -- inCombat = auto-attack active, onHateList = on something's aggro list; a world -- entry resets both (the ref's own PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD arm). The repaint itself -- rides the shared Update below — this file's posture (the PvP sound note). if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" then frame.inCombat = nil frame.onHateList = nil elseif event == "PLAYER_ENTER_COMBAT" then frame.inCombat = 1 elseif event == "PLAYER_LEAVE_COMBAT" then frame.inCombat = nil elseif event == "PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED" then frame.onHateList = 1 elseif event == "PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED" then frame.onHateList = nil end BenillaUnitFrame_Update(frame) -- The player's flag-change sound (decision 0646 §2/§4). The reference plays -- igPVPUpdate inside PlayerFrame_UpdatePvPStatus's two show branches, which it only -- ever reaches from UNIT_FACTION; our repaint runs from the shared Update on every -- event, so the sound rides the (edge-fired) event instead of the repaint — one -- sound per real flag change, which is what the reference audibly does. if event == "UNIT_FACTION" and frame.unit == "player" and frame.pvpShown then PlaySound("igPVPUpdate") end end
-- The PvP flag icon (decision 0646 §4). The reference writes this law twice with -- identical branches — PlayerFrame_UpdatePvPStatus (ref-PlayerFrame.lua l.55-79) and the -- tail of TargetFrame_CheckFaction (ref-TargetFrame.lua l.193-202) — so it lives once -- here. Branch ORDER is the reference's and it is load-bearing: free-for-all wins -- outright (an FFA-flagged player shows the FFA skull even while ordinarily flagged), and -- the faction leg needs BOTH a resolvable side and the flag. `frame.pvpShown` is what the -- caller sounds off. function BenillaUnitFrame_UpdatePvP(frame) local icon = frame.pvpIcon if not icon then return end local unit = frame.unit local texture if UnitIsPVPFreeForAll(unit) then texture = "Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-PVP-FFA" else local factionGroup = UnitFactionGroup(unit) if factionGroup and UnitIsPVP(unit) then texture = "Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-PVP-" .. factionGroup end end frame.pvpShown = texture ~= nil if texture then icon:SetTexture(texture) icon:Show() else icon:Hide() end end
-- ── Combat feedback: the portrait hit indicator (decision 0576) ────────────────────── -- Ref CombatFeedback.lua, transcribed onto frame-param style (the ref reads `this`). -- Timings/colors/size factors verbatim. The words come from the GLOBALS, exactly as the ref -- builds this table (CombatFeedback.lua l.6-17: CombatFeedbackText["MISS"] = TEXT(MISS)), -- so a localized install shows its own — the app runs the real GlobalStrings.lua off the -- patch chain before this file (ui_script/mod.rs). The enUS literals are the fallback for -- the test harnesses, which load no patch chain. COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEINTIME = 0.2 COMBATFEEDBACK_HOLDTIME = 0.7 COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEOUTTIME = 0.3
CombatFeedbackText = { INTERRUPT = INTERRUPT or "Interrupt", MISS = MISS or "Miss", RESIST = RESIST or "Resist", DODGE = DODGE or "Dodge", PARRY = PARRY or "Parry", BLOCK = BLOCK or "Block", EVADE = EVADE or "Evade", IMMUNE = IMMUNE or "Immune", DEFLECT = DEFLECT or "Deflect", ABSORB = ABSORB or "Absorb", REFLECT = REFLECT or "Reflect", }
function CombatFeedback_OnCombatEvent(frame, event, flags, amount, type) local feedbackText = frame.feedbackText if not feedbackText then return end local fontHeight = frame.feedbackFontHeight local text = "" local r, g, b = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
if event == "IMMUNE" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 0.5 text = CombatFeedbackText[event] elseif event == "WOUND" then if amount ~= 0 then if flags == "CRITICAL" or flags == "CRUSHING" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 1.5 elseif flags == "GLANCING" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 0.75 end -- type > 0 = a spell school: the number reads yellow, physical white. if type > 0 then r, g, b = 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 end text = amount elseif flags == "ABSORB" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 0.75 text = CombatFeedbackText["ABSORB"] elseif flags == "BLOCK" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 0.75 text = CombatFeedbackText["BLOCK"] elseif flags == "RESIST" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 0.75 text = CombatFeedbackText["RESIST"] else text = CombatFeedbackText["MISS"] end elseif event == "BLOCK" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 0.75 text = CombatFeedbackText[event] elseif event == "HEAL" then text = amount r, g, b = 0.0, 1.0, 0.0 if flags == "CRITICAL" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 1.5 end elseif event == "ENERGIZE" then text = amount r, g, b = 0.41, 0.8, 0.94 if flags == "CRITICAL" then fontHeight = fontHeight * 1.5 end else text = CombatFeedbackText[event] end
frame.feedbackStartTime = GetTime()
feedbackText:SetTextHeight(fontHeight) feedbackText:SetText(text) feedbackText:SetTextColor(r, g, b) feedbackText:SetAlpha(0.0) feedbackText:Show() end
-- The fade envelope (ref CombatFeedback_OnUpdate): 0.2 s ramp in, 0.7 s hold, 0.3 s -- ramp out, then Hide. GetTime-based like the ref — no per-tick accumulation. function CombatFeedback_OnUpdate(frame) local feedbackText = frame.feedbackText if not (feedbackText and feedbackText:IsVisible()) then return end local elapsedTime = GetTime() - frame.feedbackStartTime local fadeInTime = COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEINTIME if elapsedTime < fadeInTime then feedbackText:SetAlpha(elapsedTime / fadeInTime) return end local holdTime = COMBATFEEDBACK_HOLDTIME if elapsedTime < fadeInTime + holdTime then feedbackText:SetAlpha(1.0) return end local fadeOutTime = COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEOUTTIME if elapsedTime < fadeInTime + holdTime + fadeOutTime then feedbackText:SetAlpha(1.0 - (elapsedTime - holdTime - fadeInTime) / fadeOutTime) return end feedbackText:Hide() end
-- Pull the unit's current state and repaint. A non-existent unit hides the whole frame. -- The classification border art (TargetFrame_CheckClassification, ref-TargetFrame.lua -- l.205-218) — transcribed branch for branch, and the shape is the surprise: 1.12 has FIVE -- classifications but only THREE border textures, because elite, rareelite and worldboss all -- take the same Elite art. There is no rare-elite border in this build and no rare-elite -- tooltip word either (the level line's rank table is {"", ELITE, ELITE, BOSS, ""}), so -- "rareelite" is a distinction the API makes and the pixels never do. Verified rather than -- assumed, because later expansions DO ship UI-TargetingFrame-Rare-Elite and it would be the -- natural thing to write: that path is absent from 1.12's patch chain entirely, and the ref -- Lua sends rareelite to the Elite art. -- -- SetTexture is the whole operation — no TexCoords, size or anchor changes. That is only -- sound because all three BLPs are 256x128 (checked, not assumed), so the region's -- XML-declared TexCoords (0.09375..1.0 x 0..0.78125 = the 232x100 crop) frame all three -- identically, and our SetTexture touches only the path (it leaves tex_coords alone). function BenillaTargetFrame_CheckClassification(frame) local classification = UnitClassification(frame.unit) if classification == "worldboss" or classification == "rareelite" or classification == "elite" then frame.frameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-TargetingFrame-Elite") elseif classification == "rare" then frame.frameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-TargetingFrame-Rare") else frame.frameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-TargetingFrame") end end
function BenillaUnitFrame_Update(frame) local unit = frame.unit if not UnitExists(unit) then frame:Hide() return end frame:Show()
frame.healthBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, UnitHealthMax(unit)) frame.healthBar:SetValue(UnitHealth(unit))
local maxPower = UnitPowerMax(unit) if maxPower > 0 then frame.powerBar:Show() local _, token = UnitPowerType(unit) local c = BENILLA_POWER_COLORS[token] or BENILLA_POWER_COLORS.MANA frame.powerBar:SetStatusBarColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) frame.powerBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, maxPower) frame.powerBar:SetValue(UnitPower(unit)) else frame.powerBar:Hide() end
frame.nameText:SetText(UnitName(unit) or "Unknown")
-- The level slot (TargetFrame_CheckLevel, ref-TargetFrame.lua l.119-142): a corpse -- target or one whose level "can't be told" (UnitLevel ≤ 0 — the −1 return for a -- world boss / a hostile 10+ levels up) shows the skull instead of the number; a -- told level is difficulty-colored when the target is attackable (GetDifficultyColor, -- the same con law the V-plate paints its level with) and plain gold when not. -- The player frame has no skull region and shows its own level, always gold. local level = UnitLevel(unit) if frame.highLevel then if UnitIsCorpse(unit) or level <= 0 then frame.levelText:Hide() frame.highLevel:Show() else frame.levelText:SetText(level) if UnitCanAttack("player", unit) then local color = GetDifficultyColor(level) frame.levelText:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) else frame.levelText:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.82, 0.0) end frame.levelText:Show() frame.highLevel:Hide() end else frame.levelText:SetText(level) end
-- Tint the name/level plate (target only; TargetFrame_CheckFaction, ref-TargetFrame.lua -- l.144-191). A PLAYER-CONTROLLED target takes the player branch (l.145-174); only an NPC -- takes the reaction swatch (l.179-190): the resolved UnitReactionColor (neutral → -- yellow), or blue when the reaction can't be told (nil) — a player never reads the -- reaction green, which is why the two paths differ at all. -- The player branch runs the ref's full ladder now that the -- PvP wire carries it (decision 0646 §4): hostile red, else attackable-but-not-hostile -- yellow (l.158), else "we can assist them but they're PvP-flagged" green (l.163), else -- blue. Only the tapped-by-other grey (l.176) is still deferred — it needs the tap wire. -- The ref's first leg tests mutual attackability (UnitCanAttack both ways); our -- UnitCanAttack carries only the player→unit direction, so UnitIsEnemy (reaction ≤ 2) -- stands in for it — the same substitution this branch has always made. (The ref gates on -- UnitPlayerControlled, which also covers pets; UnitIsPlayer is the player half we can -- resolve — see the header deviation.) if frame.nameBackground then if UnitIsPlayer(unit) then local c if UnitIsEnemy(unit, "player") then c = BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[2] elseif UnitCanAttack("player", unit) then c = BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[4] elseif UnitIsPVP(unit) then c = BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[6] end if c then frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) else frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) end else local reaction = UnitReaction(unit, "player") local c = reaction and BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[reaction] if c then frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) else frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) end end end
-- The classification border (target only) — the ref's TargetFrame_Update calls -- CheckClassification right here, between CheckFaction and CheckDead. if frame.frameTexture then BenillaTargetFrame_CheckClassification(frame) end
-- DEAD text (target only): shown at zero health (ref TargetFrame_CheckDead). Blanked -- via SetText when alive — a site that predates region Show/Hide (region.rs has the -- real pair now, the level slot above uses it); equivalent either way. if frame.deadText then if UnitHealth(unit) <= 0 then frame.deadText:SetText("DEAD") else frame.deadText:SetText("") end end
-- The PvP flag icon, on both frames (decision 0646 §4). BenillaUnitFrame_UpdatePvP(frame)
-- The status flash, player frame only (handle-gated like pvpIcon; decision 1082). if frame.statusTexture then BenillaPlayerFrame_UpdateStatus(frame) end
-- The aura rows (target only) — the ref's TargetFrame_Update → -- TargetDebuffButton_Update: repainted on PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and UNIT_AURA alike. if unit == "target" then BenillaTargetAuras_Update() end end
-- ref TargetFrame.lua l.2-3. MAX_TARGET_DEBUFFS = 16 MAX_TARGET_BUFFS = 5
-- TargetDebuffButton_Update (ref-TargetFrame.lua l.263-387), transcribed onto the Era API -- (decision 0255: UnitBuff returns name,icon,count,debuffType,… — the 1.12 original returned -- the texture first). Only called with a live target (BenillaUnitFrame_Update guards). -- DebuffTypeColor is defined by BuffFrame.xml, which loads AFTER this file — safe, because -- this function only runs on events, never at load (no target exists at load). function BenillaTargetAuras_Update() local button local numBuffs = 0 for i = 1, MAX_TARGET_BUFFS do local name, icon = UnitBuff("target", i) button = getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameBuff" .. i) if name then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(icon or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) button:Show() numBuffs = numBuffs + 1 else button:Hide() end end
local numDebuffs = 0 for i = 1, MAX_TARGET_DEBUFFS do local name, icon, count, debuffType = UnitDebuff("target", i) button = getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. i) if name then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(icon or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) local color = DebuffTypeColor[debuffType] or DebuffTypeColor["none"] local countText = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") if count and count > 1 then countText:SetText(count) else countText:SetText("") end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Border"):SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) button:Show() numDebuffs = numDebuffs + 1 else button:Hide() end end
-- The dynamic anchors (ref l.312-331). No target-of-target frame exists yet, so its -- branches take the not-shown leg: wrap 6, buffs open under Debuff7. local targetofTarget = false local debuffWrap = 6
if UnitIsFriend("player", "target") then BenillaTargetFrameBuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaTargetFrame", "BOTTOMLEFT", 5, 32) BenillaTargetFrameDebuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaTargetFrameBuff1", "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) else BenillaTargetFrameDebuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaTargetFrame", "BOTTOMLEFT", 5, 32) BenillaTargetFrameBuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaTargetFrameDebuff7", "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) end
-- Shrink when the debuffs would overlap the frame (ref l.340-347): 21→17 icons, -- 23→19 borders. local debuffSize, debuffFrameSize if (targetofTarget and numBuffs == 5) or numDebuffs >= debuffWrap then debuffSize = 17 debuffFrameSize = 19 else debuffSize = 21 debuffFrameSize = 23 end
for i = 1, 5 do button = getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameBuff" .. i) button:SetWidth(debuffSize) button:SetHeight(debuffSize) end -- The ref resizes only the FIRST ROW's debuffs (l.358-368) — rows 2+ stay 17px always. for i = 1, 6 do button = getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. i) local border = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Border") border:SetWidth(debuffFrameSize) border:SetHeight(debuffFrameSize) button:SetWidth(debuffSize) button:SetHeight(debuffSize) end
-- Re-seat the wrap points (ref l.370-385) — constant with wrap pinned at 6, kept -- verbatim so the ToT wrap-5 leg drops in unchanged. getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. debuffWrap):ClearAllPoints() getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. debuffWrap):SetPoint("LEFT", getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. (debuffWrap - 1)), "RIGHT", 3, 0) getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. (debuffWrap + 1)):ClearAllPoints() getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. (debuffWrap + 1)):SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaTargetFrameDebuff1", "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. (debuffWrap + 2)):ClearAllPoints() getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. (debuffWrap + 2)):SetPoint("LEFT", getglobal("BenillaTargetFrameDebuff" .. (debuffWrap + 1)), "RIGHT", 3, 0) if debuffWrap == 5 then BenillaTargetFrameDebuff11:ClearAllPoints() BenillaTargetFrameDebuff11:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "BenillaTargetFrameDebuff6", "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) else BenillaTargetFrameDebuff11:ClearAllPoints() BenillaTargetFrameDebuff11:SetPoint("LEFT", "BenillaTargetFrameDebuff10", "RIGHT", 3, 0) end end
-- The aura hover (ref TargetDebuffButtonTemplate/TargetBuffButtonTemplate OnEnter, -- l.60-62/l.79-81): the aura tooltip, seated BOTTOMRIGHT of the button. function BenillaTargetAuraButton_OnEnter(button, harmful) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_BOTTOMRIGHT", 15, -25) if harmful then GameTooltip:SetUnitDebuff("target", button:GetID()) else GameTooltip:SetUnitBuff("target", button:GetID()) end end
-- The status flash's paint (ref PlayerFrame_UpdateStatus, transcribed onto frame-param -- style; decision 1082). Priority is the ref's: RESTING wins over combat — sitting in an -- inn mid-auto-attack shows the zzz — then the auto-attack state (gold ring/zzz vs red -- ring/swords/red disc), then bare swords for on-someone's-aggro-list, then nothing. function BenillaPlayerFrame_UpdateStatus(frame) if IsResting() then frame.statusTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.88, 0.25, 1.0) frame.statusTexture:Show() frame.restIcon:Show() frame.attackIcon:Hide() frame.restGlow:Show() frame.attackGlow:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Show() frame.attackBackground:Hide() elseif frame.inCombat then frame.statusTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0) frame.statusTexture:Show() frame.attackIcon:Show() frame.restIcon:Hide() frame.attackGlow:Show() frame.restGlow:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Show() frame.attackBackground:Show() elseif frame.onHateList then frame.attackIcon:Show() frame.restIcon:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Hide() frame.attackBackground:Hide() else frame.statusTexture:Hide() frame.restIcon:Hide() frame.attackIcon:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Hide() frame.attackBackground:Hide() end end
-- ref PlayerFrame_OnUpdate: the status pulse — a 0.5 s triangle wave between alpha -- 55/255 and 255/255 on the ADD-blend status ring and the icon glow, run only while the -- ring is visible (resting or auto-attacking); the hit-indicator fade rides the same -- tick, exactly as before. function BenillaPlayerFrame_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) if frame.statusTexture:IsVisible() then local counter = frame.statusCounter + elapsed local sign = frame.statusSign if counter > 0.5 then sign = -sign frame.statusSign = sign end counter = mod(counter, 0.5) frame.statusCounter = counter local alpha if sign == 1 then alpha = (55 + counter * 400) / 255 else alpha = (255 - counter * 400) / 255 end frame.statusTexture:SetAlpha(alpha) frame.statusGlow:SetAlpha(alpha) end CombatFeedback_OnUpdate(frame) end
-- Left-click the player frame to target yourself (ref PlayerFrame_OnClick, the LeftButton -- branch: an item on the cursor auto-equips, otherwise TargetUnit("player")); right-click -- opens the SELF menu (ref's ToggleDropDownMenu at (106, 27), decision 0434 phase 5). The -- ref's frame is a Button; ours is a mouse-enabled Frame, which fires OnClick on release -- with arg1 = the button. The self-target itself is the byte-verified way the client -- selects its own unit; the world-model click is a separate path, deliberately left out -- (director's call). function BenillaPlayerFrame_OnClick(button) if button == "RightButton" then ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, PlayerFrameDropDown, "BenillaPlayerFrame", 106, 27) return end if button ~= "LeftButton" then return end if CursorHasItem() then AutoEquipCursorItem() else TargetUnit("player") end end
-- The right-click dropdowns (decision 0434 phase 5; ref TargetFrame.lua l.431-455, -- PlayerFrame.lua l.235-241): MENU displayMode over the shared kit (UIDropDownMenu.xml), -- the menus themselves from UnitPopup.xml. The menu pick is the ref's law: self → SELF, -- party member → PARTY, other player → PLAYER, NPC → the bare raid-target icon list. function TargetFrameDropDown_OnLoad() UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(this, TargetFrameDropDown_Initialize, "MENU") end
function TargetFrameDropDown_Initialize() local menu local name if UnitIsUnit("target", "player") then menu = "SELF" elseif UnitIsUnit("target", "pet") then -- Selecting your own pet and right-clicking the TARGET frame gives you the pet -- menu — the ref's own second branch (TargetFrame.lua l.440-441), which sat as a -- comment here until the "pet" token (0990) and then the menu itself (1066). menu = "PET" elseif UnitIsPlayer("target") then if UnitInParty("target") then menu = "PARTY" else menu = "PLAYER" end else menu = "RAID_TARGET_ICON" name = RAID_TARGET_ICON end if menu then UnitPopup_ShowMenu(TargetFrameDropDown, menu, "target", name) end end
function PlayerFrameDropDown_OnLoad() UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(this, PlayerFrameDropDown_Initialize, "MENU") end
function PlayerFrameDropDown_Initialize() UnitPopup_ShowMenu(PlayerFrameDropDown, "SELF", "player") end
-- ref TargetFrame_OnClick: right-click opens the unit menu at (120, 10). The ref's -- LeftButton branch (SpellTargetUnit / DropItemOnUnit) rides the spell-cursor and -- item-drop slices — a bare left-click is a no-op on the ref too. function BenillaTargetFrame_OnClick(button) if button == "RightButton" then ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, TargetFrameDropDown, "BenillaTargetFrame", 120, 10) end end

Scripts.OnShow: if UnitIsEnemy("target", "player") then PlaySound("igCreatureAggroSelect") elseif UnitIsFriend("player", "target") then PlaySound("igCharacterNPCSelect") else PlaySound("igCreatureNeutralSelect") end

function BenillaPetFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame.portrait = BenillaPetFrameTextureFramePortrait frame.healthBar = BenillaPetFrameHealthBar frame.manaBar = BenillaPetFrameManaBar frame.nameText = BenillaPetFrameTextureFrameName -- The recessed-bar look, the same mechanism the player/target/party frames use -- (decision 0884): push the bars one frame level BELOW the art's TextureFrame, because -- the draw layer is bucket-wide and the frame level is the one key term above it. local level = BenillaPetFrameTextureFrame:GetFrameLevel() frame.healthBar:SetFrameLevel(level - 1) frame.manaBar:SetFrameLevel(level - 1) frame.attackModeCounter = 0 frame.attackModeSign = -1 frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_PET") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_AURA") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXHEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_POWER_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_NAME_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_ATTACK_START") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_ATTACK_STOP") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HAPPINESS") frame:EnableMouse(true) BenillaPetFrame_Update(frame) end
-- ref PetFrame_OnEvent, with both of its argument gates kept: UNIT_PET names the OWNER -- ("player" — wow-re §9 carves the arg), every other UNIT_* names the pet itself. Getting -- those backwards is how a pet frame ends up repainting off the player's health. function BenillaPetFrame_OnEvent(frame) if event == "PET_ATTACK_START" then BenillaPetFrameAttackMode:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) BenillaPetFrameAttackMode:Show() return elseif event == "PET_ATTACK_STOP" then BenillaPetFrameAttackMode:Hide() return elseif event == "UNIT_HAPPINESS" then -- The ref's own last arm: repaint the icon alone, not the whole frame. BenillaPetFrame_SetHappiness() return elseif event == "UNIT_PET" then if arg1 ~= "player" then return end elseif string.sub(event, 1, 5) == "UNIT_" and arg1 ~= "pet" then return end BenillaPetFrame_Update(frame) end
function BenillaPetFrame_Update(frame) if not UnitExists("pet") then frame:Hide() return end frame:Show() SetPortraitTexture(frame.portrait, "pet") frame.nameText:SetText(UnitName("pet") or "")
frame.healthBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, UnitHealthMax("pet")) frame.healthBar:SetValue(UnitHealth("pet"))
-- The ref's art swap (PetFrame.lua's Update): a powerless pet wears the -NoMana plate, -- which has no mana rail to leave empty. The bar hides with it, as on every other frame. local maxPower = UnitPowerMax("pet") if maxPower > 0 then BenillaPetFrameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-SmallTargetingFrame") frame.manaBar:Show() local _, token = UnitPowerType("pet") local c = BENILLA_POWER_COLORS[token] or BENILLA_POWER_COLORS.MANA frame.manaBar:SetStatusBarColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) frame.manaBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, maxPower) frame.manaBar:SetValue(UnitPower("pet")) else BenillaPetFrameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-SmallTargetingFrame-NoMana") frame.manaBar:Hide() end
BenillaPetFrame_UpdateDebuffs() BenillaPetFrame_SetHappiness() end
-- ref PetFrame_SetHappiness (PetFrame.lua l.132-156), quoted (decision 1005). -- -- `GetPetHappiness` hands back a PRE-BUCKETED 1/2/3 — the client does the thresholding -- against PetPersonality.dbc, not this function — plus the two numbers that bucket -- selects. Three things here are load-bearing and each is the reference's own: -- * the hide test is `not happiness or not isHunterPet`, so a bucket of **0** (truthy in -- Lua) leaves the icon SHOWING with whatever texcoords it had. Testing `happiness == 0` -- or coercing 0 to nil would hide a frame the reference shows. -- * the three texcoord cuts run 3/2/1 left-to-right across the strip — happy is at x=0. -- * the loyalty line is chosen by the SIGN of loyaltyRate, which is why that return is -- unscaled and allowed to be negative. function BenillaPetFrame_SetHappiness() local happiness, damagePercentage, loyaltyRate = GetPetHappiness() local hasPetUI, isHunterPet = HasPetUI() if not happiness or not isHunterPet then BenillaPetFrameHappiness:Hide() return end BenillaPetFrameHappiness:Show() if happiness == 1 then BenillaPetFrameHappinessTexture:SetTexCoord(0.375, 0.5625, 0, 0.359375) elseif happiness == 2 then BenillaPetFrameHappinessTexture:SetTexCoord(0.1875, 0.375, 0, 0.359375) elseif happiness == 3 then BenillaPetFrameHappinessTexture:SetTexCoord(0, 0.1875, 0, 0.359375) end BenillaPetFrameHappiness.tooltip = getglobal("PET_HAPPINESS" .. happiness) BenillaPetFrameHappiness.tooltipDamage = format(PET_DAMAGE_PERCENTAGE, damagePercentage) if loyaltyRate < 0 then BenillaPetFrameHappiness.tooltipLoyalty = getglobal("LOSING_LOYALTY") elseif loyaltyRate > 0 then BenillaPetFrameHappiness.tooltipLoyalty = getglobal("GAINING_LOYALTY") else BenillaPetFrameHappiness.tooltipLoyalty = nil end end
-- The four debuff buttons (ref PetFrame.xml's $parentDebuff1..4 over RefreshBuffs). The pet -- carries no aura timers — no unit but yourself does on the 1.12 wire (decision 0257 B6) — -- so these are icon + border + stack count, the party rows' shape exactly. function BenillaPetFrame_UpdateDebuffs() for i = 1, 4 do local button = getglobal("BenillaPetFrameDebuff" .. i) local _, icon, count = UnitDebuff("pet", i) if icon then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(icon) local text = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") if count and count > 1 then text:SetText(count) text:Show() else text:Hide() end button:Show() else button:Hide() end end end
-- ref PetFrame_OnUpdate: the attack overlay's alpha ramp — a 0.5 s-per-leg triangle between -- 55/255 and 1, sign-flipped at each end (the ref's own counter shape, transcribed). function BenillaPetFrame_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) if not BenillaPetFrameAttackMode:IsVisible() then return end local counter = frame.attackModeCounter + elapsed local sign = frame.attackModeSign if counter > 0.5 then sign = -sign frame.attackModeSign = sign end counter = math.fmod(counter, 0.5) frame.attackModeCounter = counter local alpha if sign == 1 then alpha = (55 + (counter * 400)) / 255 else alpha = (255 - (counter * 400)) / 255 end BenillaPetFrameAttackMode:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, alpha) end
-- ref PetFrame_OnClick, now whole (decision 1066 built the right branch). Its FIRST leg is -- the one that is easy to drop: with a spell armed, a RIGHT click disarms rather than -- opening the menu, and it precedes both branches. function BenillaPetFrame_OnClick(button) if SpellIsTargeting() and button == "RightButton" then SpellStopTargeting() return end if button == "LeftButton" then if SpellIsTargeting() then SpellTargetUnit("pet") elseif CursorHasItem() then DropItemOnUnit("pet") else TargetUnit("pet") end else -- No anchor arguments, unlike the player and target frames: the ref opens this one -- at the CURSOR (PetFrame.lua l.128). ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, PetFrameDropDown) end end
-- The PET menu's owner (ref PetFrame.lua l.158-166). The UnitExists gate is the ref's own, -- and it is not redundant with the frame being hidden: this dropdown is also what the -- TARGET frame's menu falls through to when you have your own pet selected. function PetFrameDropDown_OnLoad() UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(this, PetFrameDropDown_Initialize, "MENU") end
function PetFrameDropDown_Initialize() if UnitExists("pet") then UnitPopup_ShowMenu(PetFrameDropDown, "PET", "pet") end end
function BenillaPetFrame_OnEnter(frame) -- The pet frame is a unit frame in the reference, and takes the same cursor split: -- hovering it with a spell armed lights or greys exactly as the target frame does. if SpellIsTargeting() then if SpellCanTargetUnit("pet") then SetCursor("CAST_CURSOR") else SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end end if not UnitExists("pet") then return end GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, frame) if GameTooltip:SetUnit("pet") then getglobal("GameTooltipTextLeft1"):SetTextColor(GameTooltip_UnitColor("pet")) end end

Scripts.OnEnter: if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:SetOwner(this, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetUnitDebuff("pet", this:GetID()) end

if this.tooltip then GameTooltip:SetOwner(this, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetText(this.tooltip) if this.tooltipDamage then GameTooltip:AddLine(this.tooltipDamage, "", 1, 1, 1) end if this.tooltipLoyalty then GameTooltip:AddLine(this.tooltipLoyalty, "", 1, 1, 1) end GameTooltip:Show() end
